scope: A01 direct append builtin; production whitelist changes, unit tests, CLI acceptance, website fixtures and QA classifications
environment: Mac native darwin/arm64, Go 1.27.1, GOTOOLCHAIN=local, dependencies offline

production.assessment: Two existing len/cap dispatch lists now include append. Template-local and definition-site function handling retain precedence. Existing compiler-owned marker restoration emits native append and introduces no wrapper, new argument evaluation or storage operation. No blocking finding.

independent_validation: Real CLI and native Go run: slice header mutated by subsequent ? operand; None leaves backing storage unchanged; string spread with ?; first-operand ? suppresses later operand; named-result and range-closure append shadows passed
Cross-file macro definition plus caller import named append, Option syntax and ? forced late marker restoration; real directory CLI and native runtime emitted x yy
Real CLI build rejected captured untyped nil base, byte overflow, string spread into []rune, mixed ellipsis, and go append result discard
15 baseline/current diagnostic controls compare restored 771d464 CLI against current CLI on identical Go 1.27.1, including generated Go and exact source-map segments

diagnostic_boundary.classification: existing A03 boundary, not an append regression
diagnostic_boundary.baseline_controls: Old and current len/cap capture errors and ordinary function capture errors all point at generated '(' with no Origin. Direct native append errors retain source positions in both versions.
diagnostic_boundary.append_controls: Non-slice, wrong-element, spread, and mixed-spread errors point at generated capture '('; append() points at original template append token and retains macro stack.
diagnostic_boundary.test_revision: Current acceptance assertions require rejection reason plus generated/unmapped only for identified synthetic-argument cases. Missing-slice and macro-binding failures retain original file/line and definition/call-stack assertions.

website_review: Five positive fixtures cover native storage, bindings, string spread, question propagation and definition-site function binding. Six frontend binding rejects require exact CLI/WASM diagnostic parity, empty output, disabled copy, and successful subsequent compilation. Four nativeTypeReject fixtures require CLI/WASM generated-Go equality followed by actual native Go build rejection with the expected diagnostic class. The result JSON explicitly states that WASM performs transpilation only for those four cases.
limits: Independent review did not repeat the full-tree race/vet/design or browser execution; those are owned by the parent and validation agents. No Linux execution claimed. No repository file changes, installs, commits or pushes performed by this reviewer.
